items.text: unknowncheats-ac published: Why is Scylla still the go-to dumper instead of PE-sieve for reversing?
items.title: Why is Scylla still the go-to dumper instead of PE-sieve for reversing?
items.content:
Hey everyone,
I've noticed that across almost every tutorial and thread regarding dumping packed/protected binaries for static analysis (IDA / Ghidra), people consistently recommend using Scylla (usually via x64dbg).
At the same time, tools like PE-sieve exist, which can dump and automatically unmap the PE (/dmode 2) without even attaching a debugger or having to deal with basic anti-debugging checks.
Is the widespread use of Scylla mainly just tradition/habit because most older stickied guides were written around it, or does Scylla actually have distinct technical advantages over PE-sieve when it comes to:
Resolving and rebuilding heavily obfuscated or redirected Import Address Tables (IAT)?
Handling specific packers/protectors (e.g., custom stubs, manual entry point alignment)?
Precision control over search/IAT recreation ranges compared to automated heuristics?
Would love to hear your experiences on which workflow produces cleaner, more reliable dumps for IDA in practice.
Thanks!
